channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx: the best frontier AI model scores just 12% across 11 real-world domains
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: SemiAnalysis published GDPx on November 2, 2026, an agentic benchmark spanning 11 high-value domains built with 14 specialist partners. Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 12.0%, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon at 10.9% and GPT-6 Astra at 9.6% — and every model scores 0% on finance and legal.

item.title: Bahrain’s sovereign fund and ARP Group plan an AI-native wholesale bank — in-principle approval in hand, final authorisation still to come
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Bahrain Mumtalakat Holding Company and ARP Group announced on November 1, 2026 that they will establish an AI-native, blockchain-enabled wholesale bank headquartered in Bahrain. The venture has in-principle approval from the Central Bank of Bahrain and will begin regulated activities only after final authorisation.

item.title: Find the file you only half-remember: hands-on with Kensaku, local search with OCR and MCP
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Kensaku (yjid/kensaku, MIT, 480 GitHub stars) is a free, local-first file launcher for Windows, macOS and Linux that searches file names, text inside documents, and text inside screenshots with OCR — nothing leaves your machine. This guide installs the v1.0.11 release and its command-line companion, runs the first scan, searches the way you remember things, and gives an AI agent the same index over MCP, read-only by default.

item.title: OpenAI plans ‘speed limits’ for the most powerful AI — and wants data centres renamed ‘AI compute campuses’
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Axios reported on November 1, 2026 that OpenAI is preparing a policy and public-relations push for after Tuesday’s midterm elections, centred on mandatory ‘speed limits’ for the most powerful AI systems and renaming data centres ‘AI compute campuses.’ Chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane said the proposals have been stockpiled since August.

item.title: Run a 763-billion-parameter model from your SSD: hands-on with InferSSD
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: InferSSD (wici-ai/inferssd, Apache-2.0, 206 GitHub stars) streams the experts of a 763-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model from SSD instead of holding them in RAM or VRAM. This guide installs it on Apple Silicon or Linux with NVIDIA CUDA, starts DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in terminal chat, serves it behind a browser UI and an OpenAI-compatible API, and states the 470 GiB download and the slow decode plainly.

item.title: Wysera launches a brand-voice AI agent: marketing drafts that sound like the company, held for human approval
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Wysera launched an AI agent on November 1, 2026 that drafts email, social posts, articles and replies from a versioned brand-voice document — and holds every draft for human approval before anything publishes. The company says 42 teams are already using it.

item.title: Fujitsu launches AI incident response in Japan: threat reports in a day, forensics in two — with experts checking the AI’s work
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Fujitsu launched a retainer-based incident response service in Japan on November 1, 2026, pairing a 24/7 frontier-AI threat analysis system with security experts: threat-analysis reports in as little as one business day, forensic reports in two.

item.title: Aramco takes 49% of HUMAIN: $2.6 billion in cash plus AI assets as Saudi Arabia consolidates its AI bet
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Aramco closed a deal for a 49% stake in HUMAIN on November 1, 2026, contributing about SAR 9.9 billion ($2.6 billion) in cash in 2026 plus AI, compute and digital assets, while Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund retains 51%.

item.title: Give your Android phone an agent that works in the background: hands-on with Mika
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Mika (wangzan101/Mika, Apache-2.0, 3,350 GitHub stars) is an on-device AI agent for Android that works your apps and the web on a hidden background screen while you keep using your phone. This guide installs the v0.1.31 APK, connects a model, pairs wireless debugging with Mika’s six-step wizard, proves it with a safe first task, and shows the adb install route from a computer.

item.title: Selljam AI goes live: one workspace for research, writing, images and publishing — from $9 a month
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Selljam AI launched on November 1, 2026, combining research, writing, image creation and publishing in one workspace built around a Brand Guide generated from a business's website. Monthly plans start at $9, with pay-as-you-go credit packs from $5.

item.title: Nace AI open-sources Drex Max v1: its 27B decision model now runs on your own hardware
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nace AI has released the open weights of Drex Max v1, a dense 27-billion-parameter decision model that returns probabilities instead of generating text. The bf16 weights, a Q8_0 GGUF and an affine Q4 checkpoint run on NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon Macs, with local Mac and CPU paths limited to text.

item.title: South Korea's exports nearly doubled in October as AI chip demand surged: $115.28 billion, $56.44 billion of it semiconductors
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: South Korea's exports rose 93.7% year on year to $115.28 billion in October, the trade ministry said on November 1, as semiconductor exports jumped 259.4% to $56.44 billion on continued AI infrastructure investment by global technology firms.

item.title: Context Labs launches AI Distillery, a Context Engine for sovereign AI on data enterprises own
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Context Labs launched the AI Distillery on November 1, a Context Engine that turns enterprise operational and business data into a governed Context Package with verified lineage, usable with any frontier or open-weight model inside the customer's own environment. It is available now through the Microsoft Marketplace.

item.title: Skip the sprite sheet: hands-on with pixelfx, 244 pixel-art game effects written as code
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: pixelfx (patch-gg/pixelfx, MIT, 1,717 GitHub stars) is 244 pixel-art game effects and animations, each a small piece of JavaScript — no image files. This guide installs it, plays a frost nova on canvas, recolors a torch, exports a sprite sheet for Godot, Unity or Phaser, plays a full acted sword move, and builds a new effect with its Claude Code skill.

item.title: Careflick opens reservations for Oak1, a pendant AI wearable for older adults
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Careflick opened reservations on November 1 for Oak1, a pendant-or-clip wearable that takes spoken requests and coordinates rides, appointments and refills through connected services, with shipping expected to begin in January 2027.

item.title: One tiny board for you and your coding agents: hands-on with Kanzo
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Kanzo 0.2.1 (emanuele-em/kanzo, AGPL-3.0, 216 GitHub stars) is a self-hosted kanban board and MCP server in one small Rust program: the whole board is one folder, a private git repo syncs it between machines, and coding agents work the same cards you do. This guide installs it, runs the board, connects Claude Code and Codex, and syncs it to a second machine.

item.title: DeepSeek's super-agent: one always-on router, many silent workers — and human attention as the real bottleneck
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DeepSeek's Harness team published a super-agent design on October 31 that replaces single chat sessions with a resident router dispatching isolated worker sessions, alongside a prototype on GitHub under the MIT license.

item.title: Presentations.AI turns Google Docs, Word and webpages into slides in under a minute — with a free Chrome extension
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Presentations.AI announced on October 31 that Google Docs, Word documents, PDFs, Notion pages, spreadsheets and webpages can now be converted into branded, editable presentations of 10 to 50 slides in under a minute, alongside a free Chrome extension that turns the webpage you are reading into a deck in one click.

item.title: Dataline announces a $10.6M seed round for agent-payable data — with a token sale to follow
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Dataline announced on October 31 a $10.6 million seed round — closed in April, the company told The Block — for a decentralized network that lets AI agents buy data per call, with a confidence score on every response. A public token sale on Base is planned by year-end.

item.title: Make your AI-built UI stop looking AI-built: hands-on with unslop, the Claude skill that redlines like a designer
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: unslop (heydamir/unslop, CC BY 4.0, 3,104 GitHub stars) is a Claude Code skill by designer Damir Sokolovsky that turns vibecoded, AI-looking interfaces into designed ones: it audits the slop, sets a five-line direction drawn from the product itself, then fixes spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion in nine ordered passes. This guide installs it, runs it on the bundled EmberAI dashboard example, takes it to a live site, and renders the optional story video.

item.title: Apple Intelligence officially comes to China: November 4 beta brings Alibaba's Qwen to Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Apple confirmed on October 31, 2026 that the first Apple Intelligence features will reach users in China, entering developer-beta testing on November 4 and shipping publicly with iOS 27.3 in December, with Alibaba's Qwen available inside Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence — but without Siri AI or the other next-generation features announced at WWDC 2026.

item.title: Turn PDFs and phone photos into Markdown on your own machine: hands-on with MiniCPM-OCR
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (OpenBMB/MiniCPM-OCR, Apache-2.0, 707 GitHub stars) is a 1.3B model that parses PDFs and images into Markdown — text, tables, formulas, and charts — with a second model, MiniCPM-OCR Jev, that scores each region for correctness. This guide runs it locally through Ollama, parses a first document with the minicpmvocr SDK, and shows the vLLM path for heavier batches.

item.title: Tanatasa lets AI assistants do the shopping in Singapore: 42,000 products via MCP, API and ChatGPT plugin
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Singapore retailer Tanatasa launched an agent-first store on October 31, 2026, letting personal AI assistants search more than 42,000 products, build carts and prepare checkout through MCP, REST APIs, CLI tools and a ChatGPT plugin — with the shopper approving the basket before payment.

item.title: One Python call drives your browser, desktop, or phone: hands-on with AutoCua
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: AutoCua (ComputerUseAgent/AutoCua, MIT) drives a browser, a desktop, or a phone from one run_agent call, with 48 model names across nine providers. This guide installs it, runs a read-only web task, branches on the result, and switches surfaces — without letting the agent near your real accounts.

item.title: Claude Ultra drops the five-hour limit: Anthropic renames Max 20x, keeps the $200 price and the weekly cap
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic renamed its Claude Max plans on October 30: Max 20x becomes Ultra at $200 a month, with the rolling five-hour usage limit removed for verified accounts. Max 5x becomes Max at $100. Prices are unchanged, weekly limits stay in place, and newer Ultra accounts keep a temporary limit until verified.
